subject: health
title: Safe Outside
about: Crossing streets, seatbelts and the back seat, helmets, water and boats, the playground, and what to do if he gets lost, all taught as calm habits rather than warnings. NC 1.PCH.2.1 (situations that cause injury) plus safe play with little reminding from PE (PE.1.PR.4.3).
tip: On your next walk, let him be the one who says stop, look and listen at the curb.

cards.q: Before you cross a street, what do you do?
cards.note: Stop at the curb. Look. Listen for cars. Then cross.

cards.q: Which way do you look before crossing?
cards.note: Look left, then right, then left again before you step off the curb.

cards.q: Where is the safe place to cross a street?
wrong: in the middle of the road
cards.note: Crosswalks are where drivers know to look for people walking.

cards.q: What do you buckle every time you ride in a car?
cards.note: Buckle up before the car moves, every single ride.

cards.q: Where do kids your age sit in a car?
cards.note: In North Carolina, kids under 8 years old and under 80 pounds ride in a car seat or booster seat.

cards.q: What keeps your head safe when you ride a bike or scooter?
cards.note: North Carolina law says kids under 16 wear a bike helmet.

cards.q: Where is it safe to swim?
wrong: where no one can see you
cards.note: A grown-up watches the water the whole time you swim.

cards.q: What do you wear on a boat?
cards.note: A life jacket goes on before you get in the boat and stays on.

cards.q: How do you move when you are next to the pool?
cards.note: The ground by a pool is wet, so we walk.

cards.q: You get lost in a store. What do you do?
cards.a: stay where you are and ask a worker
cards.note: Stay put. Look for a worker with a name tag.

cards.q: Who is a safe person to ask for help if you are lost?
cards.a: a store worker with a name tag
wrong: someone who says come with me
cards.note: Workers with name tags and police officers are good helpers.

cards.q: A grown-up you do not know asks you to go with them. What do you do?
cards.a: say no and find your grown-up
cards.note: You always check with your own grown-up first. That is the rule.

cards.q: What should you know by heart in case you get lost?
cards.note: Practice your full name and a grown-up's phone number.

cards.q: How do you go down a slide?
cards.note: Sit down, feet first, one at a time.

cards.q: Before you throw a ball in PE, what do you check?
cards.sayQ: Before you throw a ball in gym class, what do you check?
cards.a: that no one is in the way
wrong: that you throw as hard as you can
cards.note: Look first, then throw to a friend who is ready to catch.

cards.q: A classmate falls down. What do you do?
cards.note: Getting a grown-up is the kind and safe thing to do.
